title: Prospective paper sizing experiment: does sizing by the B2 4h range forecast beat simple volatility sizing after costs?
label: PAPER SIZING EXPERIMENT - simulated fills on captured quotes. Tests position sizing only; it does not test direction, does not execute, and authorizes no entry.
frozen_by: repo 2.21 maintenance build (crypto-desk package 12.4.4). Written before any PS1 observation existed: v1 never launched (not_before 2026-10-03T00:00Z) and recorded no decision, quote or execution.

supersedes.state: retired before launch; zero observations; preserved byte-identical
changed: time accounting: elapsed holding time between fills, duration-weighted estimators, 8760 h/yr basis (v1 assumed 4h per interval)
interval return: log net return (v1 simple); simple return still recorded
execution: atomic execution sets with explicit states and recovery from an immutable input snapshot
confirmation: integrity binding verified before execution and reporting
quote validation: finite numeric strings, timestamp and symbol checks
lifecycle: explicit states, operator-only termination, no restart under the same protocol
supersedes.unchanged: question, instrument, arms, formulas, calibration constants and files, band, cap, costs, capital, start rule, missing-data rules, primary comparison, checkpoints and evidence thresholds

question: Holding the same synthetic, unlevered BTC spot long, with the same decisions and the same entry/exit/rebalance rules, does sizing each 4H interval by the registered RC1D B2 4h range forecast produce a higher after-cost Sharpe ratio than sizing by a trailing Parkinson volatility estimate at the same ex-ante risk target?

instrument.traded: BTCUSDT spot on Binance - a synthetic long-only position; cash is USDT
instrument.quote_timestamp: Binance spot depth carries no exchange timestamp: each quote records request-sent and response-received times (the book existed between them), the HTTP Date header and lastUpdateId. The modeled fill time is the receipt time.
instrument.forecast_instrument: Binance BTCUSDT perpetual (the RC1D target). Sizing a spot position with a perp range forecast is deliberate: perp and spot ranges over 4 hours are near-identical, and the VOL arm reads the same perp bars from the same RC1D input snapshot.
instrument.leverage: none; weights are capped at w_max = 1

decision_schedule: every 4H close (00, 04, 08, 12, 16, 20 UTC) for which the RC1D stream registers a 4h forecast; one decision per close

start.rule: The experiment starts at the first decision at or after not_before_utc that the deployed workflow executes; that decision and its execution time are written once to streams/ps1/launch.json. Decisions before deployment are 'not deployed', not misses. The protocol and calibration are frozen before that first observation.

policy.direction: long only, every interval (the direction never varies and is not tested)
policy.holding: one holding per arm at a time; each executed rebalance sets the holding until the next executed rebalance (no overlapping positions)

arms.VOL: w = min(w_max, sigma_star / (k_vol * sd_park_42)),  sd_park_42 = sqrt(sum_{last 42 closed 4H bars} ln(high/low)^2 / (42 * 4 ln 2)) from the RC1D input bundle of the decision
arms.B2: w = min(w_max, sigma_star / (k_b2 * point)),  point = the eligible RC1D 4h B2 point forecast (ln(high/low) units) registered for the decision

policy.control: FIXED (additional control; not the primary comparator)
policy.band_rule: at an execution, an arm trades to its target only if |w_target - w_current| > 0.05, where w_current = holding value at mid / equity at mid; otherwise it does not trade. Identical for every arm; fixed a priori, not tuned.
policy.entry_exit: Entry is the first executed rebalance; each later executed rebalance is the exit of the previous interval and the entry of the next. There is no other exit.

calibration.label: TRAINING/CALIBRATION on retained history 2024-09-23 .. 2026-09-23 (the O21 validation and holdout years); not evidence and not a holdout
calibration.method: k^2 = mean(r^2 / x^2) over calibration decisions (r = next 4H close-to-close log return, x = the arm's raw forecast); s_uncond = sqrt(mean(r^2)). Variance calibration only; no return, cost or turnover statistic was computed. Range is not a standard deviation: the Brownian relation E[ln H/L] = 1.596 sigma gives k = 0.627 for a range forecast; the calibrated k_b2 = 0.799 is used.
calibration.permitted_updates: none for the life of PS1 v1. The B2 forecasts themselves follow the RC1D stream's monthly refit (part of the forecast being tested). Any change to a constant, formula, band, cap, cost or rule is a new protocol version with a new clock.

capital.per_arm: each arm and each cost scenario has its own ledger starting at 100,000 USDT cash, 0 BTC
capital.cash: USDT; earns 0; no borrowing, no shorting
capital.marking: equity = cash + BTC x mid of the captured quote, at each execution (before trading)

execution.executable_at: max(the paper decision's confirmation on origin/main, the RC1D forecast's availability time, the decision computation's end)
execution.quote_rule: a quote is eligible only if its request was sent after executable_at; a quote captured earlier, a candle price, or any quote retrieved retrospectively is never used
execution.max_delay_rule: a decision can execute until its 4H close + 90 minutes; after that it is missed and every arm keeps its holding
execution.attempts: up to 3 quote requests per run, 5 s apart; the fallback run may retry within max_delay
execution.book_validation: every price and size a decimal string parsing to a finite number > 0 (NaN, inf, empty, negative, zero and non-string values are rejected - unknown liquidity is never treated as available); at least 5 levels per side; bids strictly descending, asks strictly ascending; best bid < best ask; lastUpdateId an integer; the source URL names symbol=BTCUSDT; t_sent < t_received and t_received - t_sent <= 10 s; the HTTP Date header, when present, within 120 s of t_received. A quote failing any check is recorded with its reasons and is ineligible.
execution.fill_model: buy: walk the captured asks for the quantity (VWAP), times (1 + slippage); sell: walk the bids, times (1 - slippage); quantity beyond the captured 20 levels fills at the last level with an extra 50 bp. Fee on the filled notional. These are simulated fills, not executions.
execution.atomicity: an execution has id <decision_id>#<quote_id>. Before any ledger row is written the job records an immutable input snapshot (decision row hash, confirmation binding hash, quote row hash, prior ledger state and its hash, protocol hash) in streams/ps1/execution_states.jsonl, then writes all six rows (3 arms x 2 scenarios) in one atomic file replacement and records 'completed' with the rows' hash. States: pending, running, completed, failed, partially_written, recovered. Only completed and recovered sets enter the ledger and every metric.
execution.recovery: an execution left pending or running is rebuilt from its snapshot (never from a new quote, never at another price): with no rows written it is completed under its own id and marked 'recovered'; with some rows written those rows stay where they are, the execution is marked 'partially_written', and the full set is rebuilt under <id>~r1 and marked 'recovered'. If the snapshot cannot be verified (quote or decision row changed, or the ledger moved on) the execution is 'failed', its decision is a missed execution, and nothing is rebuilt. A decision with a completed, recovered, running or pending execution is never executed again.
execution.confirmation_binding: each confirmation stores a binding - record_sha256 (canonical hash of the decision row), decision_utc, version (protocol version, protocol hash, job), input_snapshot (RC1D frozen-record hash and snapshot hash), contract (the RC1D contract id) - and binding_sha256. Execution and reporting recompute both; any mismatch is an integrity failure: the decision is excluded, the original rows are left untouched, and the failure is recorded in streams/ps1/integrity.jsonl.

costs.spread: paid in full by the bid/ask fill model in both scenarios
costs.source: Binance spot VIP 0 taker fee 0.1000%, as published in Binance's fee schedule and reported by secondary sources on 2026-09-30 (the primary page was not retrievable from the build container). Slippage values are assumptions. Fixed for PS1 v1.

missing_data.joint_rule: every rule below applies to all arms together: a decision is executed for all arms or for none, so no arm's comparison is selected by missing data
missing_data.missing_forecast: no eligible RC1D 4h forecast for the decision (not registered, not confirmed before its window start, or not verifiable): no rebalance for any arm; recorded 'no-rebalance: forecast unavailable'
missing_data.missing_bars: RC1D input bundle missing or failing its hash: no rebalance for any arm
missing_data.stale_forecast: a forecast is used only for its own decision; a run processing a decision after close + 90 min records it missed
missing_data.missing_quote: no eligible quote within max_delay: 'missed-execution'; every arm keeps its holding
missing_data.no_run: a scheduled decision with no decision record at all (the workflow did not run) is 'missed: no run' in the report
missing_data.delayed_start: execution delay (decision close to quote receipt) is recorded for every execution
missing_data.overlapping_windows: not possible: a single holding per arm, replaced at each execution
missing_data.incomplete_exit: an interval stays open until the next executed rebalance; if the stream pauses or ends, the open interval is 'pending' and excluded from every metric - no exit price is invented
missing_data.retries: decision ids are ps1-<decision>; a decision is executed at most once; records are append-only and idempotent

metrics.interval_return: net log return of an arm between consecutive executed rebalances, ln(pre-trade equity at fill n / pre-trade equity at fill n-1) (costs of a trade fall in the interval it opens); the simple return is recorded beside it
metrics.primary: difference in annualized after-cost Sharpe ratio, SR(B2) - SR(VOL), ordinary costs, from the duration-weighted estimators in time_accounting
secondary: realized annualized volatility vs the 15% target
paired per-interval return differences B2-VOL and B2-FIXED
all of the above under stressed costs
metrics.not_improvements: lower exposure, lower volatility or lower return alone is never reported as an improvement; realized risk and exposure are printed beside every return

time_accounting.elapsed: dt_h = (fill time n - fill time n-1) in hours, from the recorded quote receipt times; a skipped or missed decision lengthens the interval, nothing is interpolated and no intermediate return is created
time_accounting.mean: mu_h = sum(r) / sum(dt_h); annualized return = 8760 mu_h
time_accounting.variance: s2_h = sum((r - mu_h dt_h)^2) / (sum(dt_h) (n-1)/n); annualized volatility = sqrt(8760 s2_h). With equal 4h intervals this equals the sample variance of r times 2190
time_accounting.exposure: sum(w_held dt_h) / sum(dt_h), w_held = the weight set at the previous fill (no intra-interval marks)
time_accounting.flags: each interval records the decisions it spans; an interval spanning more than one 4H step is 'extended' and listed with its length

uncertainty.method: moving-block bootstrap of paired intervals (B2 and VOL (log return, dt_h) pairs resampled together), blocks of 42 intervals, 5,000 resamples, seed 20261003; 90% percentile interval of the duration-weighted Sharpe difference
uncertainty.minimum: no interval is reported below 10 complete blocks (420 executed intervals, about 70 days at full coverage)
uncertainty.dependence_note: consecutive intervals are adjacent, not overlapping; that does not make them independent (volatility clusters), hence blocks

checkpoints.C1: 180 days after launch and >= 10 blocks: descriptive report with the interval; no status change beyond 'collecting'
checkpoints.C2: 365 days after launch and >= 20 blocks: first review at which a status other than 'collecting' may be assigned

evidence.paper_supported_if: at C2 or later, all of: (a) the 90% interval of SR(B2)-SR(VOL) lies above 0 under ordinary costs; (b) the point estimate is above 0 under stressed costs; (c) at least 80% of scheduled decisions executed; (d) realized annualized volatility of both arms within 10%-20%
evidence.paper_unfavourable_if: at C2 or later, the 90% interval lies below 0 under ordinary costs
evidence.otherwise: paper-inconclusive. Failure to find a difference is not evidence that none exists.
evidence.never: No PS1 status is a trading edge, a live decision record or an entry endorsement. A paper-supported result would justify only a separately authorized, separately registered live test.

pause_terminate.refuse: the job refuses to decide or execute if this file's hash, the calibration file's hash or the calibration script's hash differs from the values the job was frozen with; refused decisions are missed
pause_terminate.terminate: see lifecycle.terminated; also when the RC1D contract is retired or the quote sources are unavailable for 14 days (recorded by the operator). PS1 v2 never restarts under the same protocol hash.

lifecycle.record: streams/ps1/lifecycle.jsonl, append-only, keyed by this protocol's sha256
lifecycle.approved: the protocol is on main: the first production run records the transition, citing the commit
lifecycle.active: set at the first completed execution
lifecycle.paused: automatic (by the job) when the last 6 scheduled decisions all failed to execute; the job keeps trying and returns to active at the next completed execution. An operator pause (by the operator) stops decisions and executions until the operator resumes.
lifecycle.terminated: operator only: a lifecycle row by the operator, or streams/ps1/terminated.json. Decisions and executions stop at once - an execution in progress is recorded failed and writes no ledger row - and the open interval stays pending. Reports keep running on the retained history.
lifecycle.archived: operator only, after termination; reports are labelled archived
lifecycle.restart: never under the same protocol hash; a new protocol version is a new stream with a new clock
lifecycle.history: no lifecycle change deletes or rewrites a record

claims_boundary: PS1 can show whether B2 sizing improved simulated after-cost risk-adjusted returns over trailing-volatility sizing for one synthetic spot policy. It cannot show a directional edge, real fill quality, capacity, or live decision performance.
